title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measure whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier with a bounded automated repair budget increases the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. For each intent a single shared_initial LLM candidate was produced and evaluated under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Outcomes: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.996667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and a repair budget ≤1 the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We release the preregistration, execution, validator traces, and analysis artifacts with the study bundle and interpret results with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational deployment policies.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to network operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent→configuration translation, configuration synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment network changes, semantic correctness—sequencing constraints, reachability, and policy preservation—is operationally critical and cannot be assured by superficial syntactic checks alone. A common engineering pattern pairs generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce operational risk. The measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends on what is held fixed (the estimand), the generator single‑shot quality, validator expressiveness, and the permitted repair budget.

We preregistered a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) to quantify deterministic rescue achievable when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. For each intent the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate (gpt-5-mini) and compared: (a) baseline — accept the single candidate without repair; and (b) guarded — run a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and allow at most one automated repair which itself is re‑validated. The primary research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus ≤1 automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair?

Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under a shared_initial estimand; (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle including validator traces and the single repair transcript archived with the run; (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation of estimator conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and system papers document a rapid increase in LLM use for NetOps tasks including intent translation, template synthesis, protocol test‑case generation, and automated repair [1–3]. Tool‑augmented and planner‑centric agent frameworks allow LLMs to call external validators or simulators and coordinate multi‑step workflows; such architectures are advocated when single‑shot generation is insufficient or when verifier‑guided decomposition is required [4,5]. Prior empirical work generally supports that introduce→validate→repair scaffolds can improve surface correctness metrics relative to unconstrained generation, but reported gains vary strongly with validator coverage, task distribution, and whether evaluations permit resampling or interactive regeneration [2,3,6].

Two methodological themes motivate our design. First, many prior evaluations conflate deterministic validation benefits with benefits from resampling (multiple independent model draws) or verifier‑guided regeneration; disentangling these requires estimand clarity [2,5]. Second, available NetOps benchmarks frequently emphasize syntactic/template correctness rather than richer semantic invariants (reachability, sequencing, policy preservation), limiting how directly experimental results transfer to operational deployment [1,7]. Our study intentionally conditions on a single shared_initial draw to isolate bounded deterministic rescue that is relevant when model calls are constrained by cost, latency, or governance.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered under id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001 and frozen before the confirmatory run. The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in the proportion of unflagged verifier passes (guarded − baseline) computed on N = 300 paired intents after applying prespecified inclusion/exclusion rules. The confirmatory analysis executor and multiplicity handling were fixed in the preregistration. (Preregistration SHA‑256 archived with the run.)

Task suite and stratification. Tasks were produced deterministically by a registered task generator into a synthetic topology suite stratified into three difficulty strata (low/medium/high). Each task encodes: the natural language intent, initial/expected final device states, required sequencing constraints, preservation invariants, and protected interfaces. The confirmatory run sampled 100 pairs per stratum (N = 300 pairs total).

Shared_initial generation and model configuration. To isolate deterministic verifier/repair rescue from resampling effects we used the shared_initial protocol: for each pair the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate (requested model: gpt-5-mini). That same candidate was reused verbatim for both baseline and guarded conditions. Model configuration parameters (declared model version and max output tokens) and the adapter family used in execution were fixed and archived with the run bundle.

Validator, scoring rule, and repair operator. Semantic evaluation used a deterministic validator implementing a full_intent_constraint_validation rule: sequencing invariants (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), required command counts, preservation of unspecified state, and forbidden changes to protected interfaces. Scoring is binary: an unflagged candidate is a pass for the estimand. The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated repair attempt (repair budget ≤ 1). The repair operator is a constrained, localized edit routine limited to sequencing insertions and similarly local edits; repairs are applied only to validator‑flagged candidates and are re‑validated deterministically.

Contamination controls and missingness. The preregistration included negative controls and deterministic contamination detection. Exclusion rules allowed pair exclusion only if both pipeline calls failed due to infrastructure outages; no such dual failures occurred in the confirmatory run and no pairs were excluded. All provider/API failures and repair traces were logged and archived.

Execution and analysis. The run used a hosted NetOps adapter under scientific_confirmatory execution mode. The confirmatory analysis used a paired exact McNemar two‑sided test on discordant counts and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000) per preregistered analysis executor. Preplanned sensitivity analyses (e.g., failure‑as‑zero) and per‑stratum diagnostics were executed as exploratory artifacts and archived. (Further low‑level provenance is archived in the run bundle.)
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The confirmatory adapter completed planned episodes yielding 300 analyzable pairs under the shared_initial protocol. Empirical model calls used = 301 (300 shared_initial generations and 1 repair invocation). Audit instrumentation recorded that the repair stage was invoked once across the 300 pairs.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667; guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test (operating on n10 and n01) returned p = 1.0. Absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01]. With total discordance m = n10 + n01 = 1 the exact test has limited sensitivity; the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point in this experimental context.

Per‑stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Per stratum tallies were: low baseline = 100/100, guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100, guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100, guarded = 100/100. The solitary discordant pair occurred in the high stratum. Validator traces attribute the initial failure to a sequencing omission: the shared_initial candidate omitted an explicit 'admin down' prior to a VLAN/MTU change mandated by the intent. The constrained repair operator inserted the missing sequencing command; revalidation reported the corrected candidate as valid, producing the deterministic rescue for that pair. The single repair trace and the validator before/after traces are archived for forensic inspection.

Missingness and contamination. Contamination checks and negative controls did not flag unexpected behavior; missingness summary reports zero failed or unscorable episodes and zero excluded pairs under preregistered rules.

Operational cost. The guarded pipeline incurred one additional repair stage call across 300 pairs (model_calls_used = 301), indicating minimal extra model‑call cost for deterministic rescue under the chosen repair budget and edit operator on this synthetic suite.
sections.discussion:
Estimand conditioning and operational interpretation. The shared_initial estimand conditions on a single LLM draw per intent and thus corresponds to operational policies that limit model calls. Under such policies the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate. Permitting resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration changes the estimand and generally increases achievable success rates by exploiting generator variance; evaluations for those policies must allow resampling and be preregistered accordingly.

Ceiling effects and pilot omission. The preregistration targeted detection of a 10 percentage‑point absolute improvement with planned power ≈0.8 based on a pilot for discordance estimation. That optional pilot was not executed, and baseline performance proved near ceiling (299/300), producing minimal discordance (m = 1) and reduced sensitivity to small absolute differences. This outcome underscores the value of small calibration pilots when generator performance may approach ceiling on selected task suites.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The observed single failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, forbidden ACL removal) were not observed at scale in this synthetic suite. The marginal utility of a guarded pipeline depends on the deployment distribution of failure modes and validator expressiveness: richer validators that check reachability or ACL semantics can increase observed rescue rates, while policies that prohibit automated edits limit the guarded pipeline to detection and human escalation.

Repair budget tradeoffs. We intentionally limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to measure bounded deterministic rescue. Iterative repair, larger edit operators, or interactive verifier‑guided generation would increase rescue opportunities but address a different estimand and operational cost profile. The archived single repair trace can inform design choices for permitted edit operators in production pipelines.

Practical implication for NetOps CI/CD. Organizations should align evaluation estimands with operational policies: when model calls are tightly budgeted, the shared_initial estimand provides a meaningful bound on deterministic verifier/repair rescue per single candidate. If multiple model calls are permitted, evaluations should measure resampling and interactive policies' benefits explicitly. In this run the guarded pipeline achieved deterministic rescue once with negligible extra model‑call cost, but the near‑ceiling baseline limits generalization of the absolute effect size.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and guarded 300/300, yielding absolute paired improvement = 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00,0.01]). Deterministic validator+repair rescued a single sequencing omission under the bounded repair budget. Because baseline single‑shot generation was near ceiling on the selected synthetic suite, the marginal observable benefit of bounded deterministic repair was small in absolute terms. We release the preregistration, execution, validator traces, repair transcript, and analysis artifacts with the study bundle to support reproducibility and targeted follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distribution, or repair budget.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
